items.b: GOLD WRITTEN BACK AT $4,643.90, THE HIGHEST MARK THIS TAPE HAS CARRIED
items.t: The Editor re-read Kitco at 05:58 New York time and wrote gold back to the tape at $4,643.90 an ounce, up $41.50 or 0.90% on Friday's $4,602.40. TradingEconomics read $4,646.92 at the same hour, a gap of $3.02 or 0.065%. Against this tape's opening mark of $4,158.30 on 5 August, gold has added $485.60, or 11.68%.

items.b: TRADINGECONOMICS CARRIES TWO GOLD FIGURES ON ONE PAGE AND WE PRINT NEITHER
items.t: The same page quotes gold live at $4,646.92 and, in its market note, at approximately $4,630, calling that a peak since mid-May. The two are $16.92 apart. This paper's mark of record is Kitco's $4,643.90, and the gap between an outside source and itself is disclosed rather than smoothed.

items.b: SILVER WRITTEN BACK AT $68.74 ON A GAP THIS TAPE STATES RATHER THAN HIDES
items.t: Kitco read silver at $68.74, down $0.12 or 0.17% from Friday's $68.86. TradingEconomics read $68.90, a gap of $0.16 or 0.23%, marginally wider than the sub-0.2% rule of thumb and the same order the tape desk accepted at 05:00. Treated as agreement and written back. The gold-to-silver ratio widens to 67.56 from 66.84.

items.b: PLATINUM AND PALLADIUM HELD FOR A THIRD SESSION ON A ONE PERCENT GAP
items.t: Kitco read platinum at $1,874.00 against TradingEconomics at $1,892.90, a gap of $18.90 or 1.01% and beyond the agreement band. The last agreed mark, $1,881.00, stands and sits inside today's live range. Palladium is held on the same basis at $1,336.00, with Kitco at $1,326.00.

items.b: GEM DIAMONDS' HALF AVERAGES $1,395 A CARAT AND THE QUARTER BEHIND IT RAN LOWER
items.t: 42,624 carats for $59.5 million in the first half, up 38% on $1,008 a year earlier, with eight stones over $1 million carrying $16.1 million of the revenue. Subtracting the first quarter's $32.1 million on 17,090 carats leaves about $27.4 million on 25,534 carats, an implied second-quarter average near $1,073.

items.b: $374 MILLION OF INDIAN JEWELLERY WENT TO AUSTRALIA AND NINE CARAT IS THE LINE
items.t: Exports rose 16% in FY2025-26 on the council's own figures, with gold jewellery up more than 28%, silver nearly 30% and coloured gemstones almost 36%. The delegation in market this week reports 9-carat gold as mainstream Australian retail and 18-carat as the premium tier. Single source, no prior-year base published.

items.b: DOHA SIGNED THREE ASIAN BOURSES IN JULY AND SAID SO THIRTY-THREE DAYS LATER
items.t: The Qatar Diamond Exchange signed memoranda with the Singapore, Shanghai and Tokyo bourses at the 41st World Diamond Congress, which closed 15 July. The statement came on 17 August and Rapaport carried it on 23 August. This paper reported the exchange's own launch on 28 July, before the agreements were public.

items.b: CORRECTION: THE LATE-JULY TARIFF ON ISRAELI GOODS IS 12.5%, NOT 10%
items.t: Sunday's Israel article said a 10% United States tariff on diamond imports took effect in late July. The 10% rate was the Section 122 tariff, which was sunsetting on or about 24 July; the measure that took effect that day was a new Section 301 forced-labour tariff, and Israel's rate under it is 12.5%. Corrected on the page and in the record.

items.b: CORRECTION: GEM DIAMONDS' $1,501 A CARAT IS A FIRST-QUARTER FIGURE
items.t: Our 29 July article and its panel gave $1,501 a carat, up about 17%, with no period label, and the 30 July Angola piece set it beside De Beers' second quarter. It is Gem Diamonds' first quarter of 2026 and was correct for that quarter. The half-year average, published 28 July, is $1,395. Labelled on both pages and in the record.
